text.name: rse_welcome_subtitle
text.text: County dispatch calls you when something goes wrong on the road.

text.name: rse_welcome_body
text.text:
Calls come on their own while you farm. Say yes, drive there, and clear the road: animals, wrecks, spilled loads, a downed power line, a flock to pen.
A call only comes if your farm has what the job takes. A pickup does the small jobs; heavy wrecks need a rollback or a big truck.
The guide explains everything, and you can open it at any time with {key:RSE_SETTINGS} on foot.

text.name: rse_welcome_pack
text.text: It needs the free Emergency Pack DLC, which is installed.

text.name: rse_welcome_beta
text.text: This is a beta. Found a bug? Report it on GitHub: github.com/Corencas/FS25_RoadsideEmergencies/issues

text.text: The vehicle is off the tracks. Now take it to the recovery point.

text.name: rse_crossing_hit
text.text: The train got there first. Nobody was hurt, but the job is lost, and there is no pay.

text.name: rse_crossing_hitFee
text.text: The train got there first. Nobody was hurt, but the job is lost. There is no pay, and you were charged %s.

text.name: rse_ep_logging_description
text.text: County dispatch: a timber trailer has overturned, and its logs are lying across the road. The owner's crew will see to the trailer; the logs are your job.

text.name: rse_logs_hint
text.text: Clear every log off the road: load them, or move them well off to the side.

text.name: rse_logs_arrived
text.text: %d logs are lying across the road.

text.name: rse_logs_progress
text.text: %d of %d pieces are clear of the road.

text.name: rse_logs_crew
text.text: The owner's crew will collect the trailer and all the logs, including any you have loaded.

text.name: rse_logs_crewLeft
text.text: The owner's crew will collect the trailer and the logs left here.

text.name: rse_logs_yours
text.text: The logs on your own vehicle are yours to keep or sell.

text.name: rse_logs_cut
text.text: The log is in two pieces now, which makes %d to clear.

text.name: rse_line_hint_wait
text.text: Wait for the county crew to arrive and cut the power. Set up cones meanwhile.

text.name: rse_line_hint_work
text.text: Recover the car and roll up each wire. Bringing the pole in is optional and pays extra.

text.name: rse_line_dangerTitle
text.text: Stay away! The wires are still live!

text.name: rse_line_dangerPay
text.text: You will reduce your pay if you stay.

text.name: rse_line_dangerPaid
text.text: Your pay has been cut for staying too close. Move back until the power is off.

text.name: rse_line_dangerCut
text.text: You stayed too close to live wires, so the county has cut your pay by %d%%.

text.name: rse_line_powerOff
text.text: County crew: the power is off, and it is safe to work.

text.name: rse_line_rollUp
text.text: Roll up wire

text.name: rse_line_stillLive
text.text: Not yet: the power is still on. The county crew needs about %d more seconds.

text.name: rse_line_wireDone
text.text: The wire is rolled up. Wires left: %d.

text.name: rse_line_pieceIn
text.text: That piece of the pole is in. Pieces left: %d.

text.name: rse_line_poleIn
text.text: The pole is in.

text.name: rse_crash_carDone
text.text: The car is in. Roll up the wires too for a %d%% bonus. If you don't, another contractor takes over after %s; the settings panel ({key:RSE_SETTINGS}) can hand them over sooner.

text.name: rse_crash_lineDone
text.text: The wires are rolled up. Bring in the car too for a %d%% bonus. If you don't, another contractor takes over after %s; the settings panel ({key:RSE_SETTINGS}) can hand it over sooner.

text.name: rse_guide_welcome_1
text.text: You are the local contractor county dispatch calls when something goes wrong on the road: animals hit by traffic, wrecked vehicles and rollovers, spilled bales, storm damage, a downed power line, a logging crash, a car in the water, a tree on a car, a vehicle stalled on a railroad crossing, and sheep loose on the road.

text.name: rse_guide_welcome_2
text.text: Roadside Emergencies needs the free Emergency Pack DLC. When you start a savegame, the game's mod list offers to select it for you. Without it, no calls come.

text.name: rse_guide_welcome_3
text.text: Open this guide at any time: press {key:RSE_SETTINGS} on foot and choose "Open the guide". The same menu has all the settings.

text.name: rse_guide_welcome_4
text.text: Every line of this mod in the F1 help starts with "RSE:", and its texts name the keys you have chosen in the game's controls menu.

text.name: rse_guide_welcome_5
text.text: The mod is for single player for now. Found a bug? Report it on GitHub: github.com/Corencas/FS25_RoadsideEmergencies/issues

text.name: rse_guide_title_tools
text.text: You only get calls you can finish

text.name: rse_guide_tools_1
text.text: This is a firm rule: if your farm doesn't have what a job takes, that call doesn't come at all. Dispatch checks every vehicle you own or lease before each call, so if the pager asks, you have what it takes.

text.name: rse_guide_tools_2
text.text: With nothing at all: deer, boar, sheep, pigs and goats in the road, which you drag by hand, and driving a flock, which you can do on foot.

text.name: rse_guide_tools_3
text.text: With a pickup truck, or any motorized vehicle of {mass:1} or more: cows, horses and buffalo, cars in the water, trees on cars, power lines, logging crashes, railroad crossings and smaller overturned trailers.

text.name: rse_guide_tools_4
text.text: With a tractor, a truck, or any motorized vehicle of {mass:3} or more: also wrecked trucks, overturned tractors, and the bigger vehicles on the other jobs.

text.name: rse_guide_tools_5
text.text: Some calls take one thing more. Big bales need a bale fork, bale grab, bale loader or forklift. Storm damage needs a trailer or a pickup bed. A livestock trailer crash needs your own livestock trailer.

text.name: rse_guide_tools_6
text.text: The pager says what a job takes before you answer. If your equipment is at the other end of the map, say no: that costs nothing.

text.name: rse_guide_title_calls
text.text: A call, step by step

text.name: rse_guide_calls_1
text.text: A pager asks whether you will take the call. It says what happened and, a line each: where it is, what is there (the animals, or the vehicle and its load), what the job takes and which of your vehicles can do it, how long you have, and about what it pays. Saying no costs nothing.

text.name: rse_guide_calls_2
text.text: Say yes and follow the marker on your map. The call panel at the right of the screen lists the job's steps and ticks each one off, and shows the way to go, the time that counts and about what the job pays. Pins over the scene show each animal or log you still have to deal with.

text.name: rse_guide_calls_3
text.text: Get there in time: a call you haven't reached after 20 minutes of play goes to another contractor, with a warning 5 minutes before (you can change the time in the settings). Once you have reached the scene, the call stays yours, except at a railroad crossing, where the train sets the clock.

text.name: rse_guide_calls_4
text.text: Traffic stops behind whatever blocks the road, so the road stays shut until you clear it. The game may take away a car that has been stuck for a long time.

text.name: rse_guide_calls_5
text.text: Only one job runs at a time. No new call comes while a job runs, or while cones or barricades of yours are still out.

text.name: rse_guide_calls_6
text.text: You can save during a job, and it comes back when you load.

text.name: rse_guide_calls_7
text.text: When a job ends, done or not, whatever is left at the scene stays until you are {distance:80} away, for at least a minute and at most 5 minutes. Then the county clears it away. Your cones and barricades, and any dead animals you loaded, are still yours to take care of.

text.name: rse_guide_title_timing
text.text: When calls come

text.name: rse_guide_timing_1
text.text: The first call can come about 5 minutes after you load. After each job there is a quiet time of at least 30, 12 or 6 minutes of play (Rarely, Normal or Often in the settings), and then a call can come at any moment.

text.name: rse_guide_timing_2
text.text: Every kind of call is as likely as any other. The bigger jobs (everything but dead animals in the road) never come within 30 minutes of each other, so on Normal one comes about once an hour.

text.name: rse_guide_timing_3
text.text: Some calls need the right place. A railroad crossing needs a map with a train that isn't rented and a crossing within reach. A car in the water needs shallow water with a gentle bank beside a road. A flock needs open country with a meadow beside the road. Storm damage only comes after a twister, from a road near where it ended, and twisters only come in spring and summer.

text.name: rse_guide_timing_4
text.text: In the settings you can turn all calls off, or only the animal calls, or only the wreck and spilled load calls.

text.name: rse_guide_title_pay
text.text: How the pay works

text.name: rse_guide_pay_1
text.text: Every job pays a set amount when it is done. The settings raise or lower all income from 50% to 200%, and the game's economy difficulty counts as well.

text.name: rse_guide_pay_2
text.text: Turn on the hazards or beacons of a vehicle of yours within {distance:40} of the scene and keep them on for 20 seconds in all: the job pays 7% more. Only lights the vehicle really has count, and not a wreck's own. You are reminded when you arrive.

text.name: rse_guide_pay_3
text.text: Dead animals moved only to the roadside pay very little. Take them to a drop-off point for the full pay; there you are also paid for the haul-off and charged a small disposal fee.

text.name: rse_guide_pay_4
text.text: A wreck pays more the farther the nearest recovery point is from the scene. Bales, logs and loose animals pay for each one brought in.

text.name: rse_guide_pay_5
text.text: Some jobs have two parts: a trailer and its bales, a livestock crash, a power line. Do both for a 25% bonus. If one part sees no progress for 10 minutes, another contractor takes it over.

text.name: rse_guide_pay_6
text.text: If you said yes and the job ends with no pay (you didn't get there in time, handed it over with nothing done, or the train got there first), you are charged a tenth of its pay. Saying no costs nothing.

text.name: rse_guide_pay_7
text.text: You can hand a job to another contractor at any time from the settings ({key:RSE_SETTINGS}). You keep the pay for what you finished, such as each bale, log or animal brought in. The row says before you choose whether you are paid, or charged.

text.name: rse_guide_title_animals
text.text: Dead animals

text.name: rse_guide_animals_1
text.text: Deer, boar, pigs, sheep and goats you can drag by hand: walk up to one and press the activate key, and again to let go. Cows, horses and water buffalo are too heavy: use the strap or a machine.

text.name: rse_guide_animals_2
text.text: An animal counts as cleared once it lies still off the road. For the full pay, load it on any vehicle and take it to a drop-off point.

text.name: rse_guide_animals_3
text.text: Animal bodies work like bales: front loaders, bale forks and grabs, cranes, trailers, tension belts and autoload mods all handle them, and the fill display counts them. A cow is heavy, so a small crane can't lift one.

text.name: rse_guide_animals_4
text.text: An animal you leave lying is marked on the map. After 30 minutes of play with nobody within {distance:20} (you can change the time in the settings), the county's road crew collects it and bills you, and takes back what the call paid you for it beyond roadside pay. You are reminded 15 and 5 minutes before.

text.name: rse_guide_animals_5
text.text: From an animal's map marker you can have the county collect it at once, for the usual bill.

text.name: rse_guide_title_points
text.text: Drop-off and recovery points

text.name: rse_guide_points_1
text.text: Dead animals go to a drop-off point; wrecks, bales and the pieces of a power pole go to a recovery point. The shop is both, and so is every point you add.

text.name: rse_guide_points_2
text.text: Add a point where you stand from the settings ({key:RSE_SETTINGS}), or remove your nearest one. Your points show on the map while you have something to bring in, and you can remove one from its map marker.

text.name: rse_guide_points_3
text.text: A dead animal counts as delivered once it has lain still for a few seconds within {distance:12} of a drop-off point, with no loader, belt or strap holding it: unload it there, or open the belts on the trailer. For a wreck, the marker on the map shows the way to the recovery point.

text.name: rse_guide_title_strap
text.text: The recovery strap

text.name: rse_guide_strap_1
text.text: On foot, aim at a dead animal or a prepared wreck and press {key:RSE_STRAP} to hook the strap exactly there. Then aim at a vehicle and press {key:RSE_STRAP} again to attach the other end. Aim at nothing to put the strap away, or at a strapped animal or wreck to take the strap off.

text.name: rse_guide_strap_2
text.text: Near a strap, hold {key:RSE_STRAP_IN} to reel it in and {key:RSE_STRAP_OUT} to let it out. It reaches {distance:20}. Hooking up pulls nothing: you reel, or you drive off.

text.name: rse_guide_strap_3
text.text: To right a wreck lying on its side, hook it high on its upper side, attach the strap to a vehicle, and pull it over. It stays where it lies until the strap goes tight.

text.name: rse_guide_strap_4
text.text: Towing: drive off with the strap tight and it closes up to a short hitch behind your vehicle. The wreck follows like a trailer, from either end, and brakes by itself when you stop. Back up and it lets go until you pull away again.

text.name: rse_guide_wrecks_1
text.text: A wrecked vehicle blocks the road. Walk up to it and prepare it for recovery, or first help out the driver, where there is one. It can't be driven, started or reset: you tow it or load it. A wreck on its side has to be righted first.

text.name: rse_guide_wrecks_2
text.text: While you reel or tow, the wheels at the end you pull turn toward the line, so that end comes straight to you. A trailer has no steering, so its wheels turn along the line while you reel.

text.name: rse_guide_wrecks_3
text.text: On a rollback: hook the strap to the wreck, attach it to the head of the bed, and hold {key:RSE_STRAP_IN}. Let it out to roll the wreck back down. Belt it down before you drive.

text.name: rse_guide_wrecks_4
text.text: Take the wreck to a recovery point to be paid; the marker shows the way. Different vehicles come from call to call, and the bigger ones come up less often.

text.name: rse_guide_title_loads
text.text: Spilled bales

text.name: rse_guide_loads_1
text.text: The call tells you what the load is. Small bales can be carried by hand, so a pickup truck is enough. Big bales pay more per bale, but they need a front loader or a telehandler.

text.name: rse_guide_loads_2
text.text: You don't need a second trip for a trailer job. Get the trailer back on its wheels, put the bales in it, and tow it all to the recovery point. A storm job has no trailer, so bring your own and make as many trips as you need.

text.name: rse_guide_loads_3
text.text: Each bale that reaches a recovery point pays, even if you hand over the rest of the job in the settings ({key:RSE_SETTINGS}). A bale pays more when the bales are all you bring in.

text.name: rse_guide_title_loose
text.text: A livestock trailer crash

text.name: rse_guide_loose_0
text.text: A livestock trailer has gone over. Two parts, in any order: the trailer to a recovery point, and the live animals into your own livestock trailer. Clear any dead ones like other dead animals.

text.name: rse_guide_loose_1
text.text: At a livestock trailer crash, live animals wander off. They stop to graze, and they shy away when you come at them.

text.name: rse_guide_loose_2
text.text: Walk up to one and use the activate key to catch it. It follows you on a lead. Bring it next to your own livestock trailer and use the key again to load it.

text.name: rse_guide_loose_3
text.text: You lead one at a time. It gets away if you run too far ahead, and it stays behind if you get in a vehicle. Once loaded, the animals are yours to sell at the animal dealer.

text.name: rse_guide_title_line
text.text: Downed power lines

text.name: rse_guide_line_1
text.text: A car has hit a utility pole. Stay back: the wires may be live, and staying too close costs you pay. A county crew drives up and cuts the power; set up your cones and lights while you wait.

text.name: rse_guide_line_2
text.text: Once the power is off, help the driver out and take the car to a recovery point. A pin shows each wire: walk up to it, anywhere along it, and hold the key to roll it up.

text.name: rse_guide_line_3
text.text: Bringing the pole in is optional and pays extra, if every piece reaches a recovery point before the rest of the job is done. It is a real log: if it has to fit on something, cut it with a chainsaw (take it out with the game's hand tool key), standing beside it and aiming across it. Do both parts, the car and the wires, for a bonus.

text.name: rse_guide_title_logs
text.text: A logging crash

text.name: rse_guide_logs_1
text.text: A logging truck has lost its load. The owner's crew sees to the trailer; your job is the logs.

text.name: rse_guide_logs_2
text.text: A log counts once it is on a truck or trailer, or lying well off the road with both ends clear of the lanes. Log forks, cranes, the strap and the chainsaw all work; a log cut in two makes two pieces to clear.

text.name: rse_guide_logs_3
text.text: When the job is done, the crew takes all the logs, also those you loaded. Hand it over early, and the logs on your vehicle are yours to keep.

text.name: rse_guide_title_crossing
text.text: A railroad crossing

text.name: rse_guide_crossing_1
text.text: A vehicle has stalled on a railroad crossing, and the map's own train is on its way: a clock shows how long you have. The call comes from a crossing within reach, with time to match the distance.

text.name: rse_guide_crossing_2
text.text: Only a strap or a winch line moves it; ramming it does nothing. Pull it clear in time, then take it to a recovery point. If the train gets there first, the job is lost and you are charged.

text.name: rse_guide_title_river
text.text: Cars in the water

text.name: rse_guide_river_1
text.text: A car has gone off the road into shallow water, with the driver inside. Wade out and help the driver out first.

text.name: rse_guide_river_2
text.text: Then hook a strap or a winch line on the car from the bank and pull it out. There is always a gentle way up. Take it to a recovery point like any other wreck.

text.name: rse_guide_river_3
text.text: These calls only come on maps that have shallow water and a gentle bank beside a road.

text.name: rse_guide_title_tree
text.text: Trees on cars

text.name: rse_guide_tree_1
text.text: A storm has dropped a tree on a car, with the driver trapped inside. Get the log off the car with a chainsaw or a strap, and the door will open so that you can help the driver out.

text.name: rse_guide_tree_2
text.text: Clear every piece off the road and take the car to a recovery point, in whichever order suits you. Get the driver out within 6 minutes of your arrival for a bonus. The logs go with the job, unless you hand it over early.

text.name: rse_guide_title_flock
text.text: Driving a flock

text.name: rse_guide_flock_1
text.text: Sheep are in bunches along the road, and the farmer has put up a pen in a meadow nearby. In a vehicle or on foot, they move straight away from you, and those beside them go along. Bring the bunches together, then steer the flock round to the gate.

text.name: rse_guide_flock_2
text.text: Press from the side opposite where you want them to go, and go round them to turn them: the flock turns away from wherever you are. Come closer and they go faster, but lean on them and one may break away, and drive fast near them and they scatter. A honk every few seconds brings each bunch a little closer together, and now and then nudges them on; lean on the horn and they scatter. Those in the pen stay in, and the farmer shuts the gate behind the last one.

text.name: rse_guide_flock_3
text.text: You need no equipment for it. The job is done when the last one is in the pen; hand it over early and you are paid for each one already in.

text.name: rse_guide_title_kit
text.text: Cones and barricades

text.name: rse_guide_kit_1
text.text: At a call, press {key:RSE_KIT_MENU} on foot to open the scene kit. {key:RSE_KIT_NEXT} picks the next item, {key:RSE_KIT_USE} places it or picks up what you aim at, and holding {key:RSE_KIT_TURN} turns it. They are free, and they stop traffic.

text.name: rse_guide_kit_2
text.text: Whatever you place, you pick up again. Until you do, the county keeps calling and no new call comes.

text.name: rse_guide_kit_3
text.text: You can place items only during a call, within {distance:60} of the scene: traffic cones, wooden barricades and cones with barrier tape. The strip at the bottom of the screen shows the one in hand, and {key:RSE_KIT_MENU} puts the kit away.

text.name: rse_guide_title_markers
text.text: Map markers

text.name: rse_guide_markers_1
text.text: A green circle with an animal is a loose animal, a red ! is a dead animal left behind, an orange cone is one of your cones or barricades, and a green ring is a farmer's pen. A blue number is your own drop-off point, shown while you have something to bring.

text.name: rse_guide_markers_2
text.text: Click a marker on the map to see what it is and teleport there. You can also have the county collect a dead animal, for the usual bill, or remove a drop-off point.

text.name: rse_guide_markers_3
text.text: Add your own drop-off points in the settings ({key:RSE_SETTINGS}).

text.name: rse_guide_markers_4
text.text: You can turn the map markers off in the settings.

text.name: rse_guide_settings_1
text.text: On foot, {key:RSE_SETTINGS} opens the settings. Up and Down choose a row, Left and Right change it, Enter confirms, and {key:RSE_SETTINGS} or Esc closes.

text.name: rse_guide_settings_2
text.text: The rows: whether dispatch calls by itself; how often calls come; animal calls; wreck and spilled load calls; job size (how many animals or bales: small, normal, large or random); income (50% to 200%); disposal fees and county bills (0% to 200%); when the county collects what you leave behind; when another contractor takes over a call you haven't reached; map markers; and the call panel.

text.name: rse_guide_settings_3
text.text: Your settings are kept with the savegame, and a new savegame starts with the ones you used last. "Return all settings to default" keeps your drop-off points.

text.name: rse_guide_title_mods
text.text: Works well with

text.name: rse_guide_mods_1
text.text: You don't need any of these mods, but they suit the work. The ones named here have been tested with Roadside Emergencies.

text.name: rse_guide_mods_2
text.text: T880 Rollback by Roughneck Modding Crew: pull a wreck onto the bed with the strap ({key:RSE_STRAP}) and the reel keys ({key:RSE_STRAP_IN} and {key:RSE_STRAP_OUT}), belt it down, and drive it in. Their International CV Rollback is confirmed to work too.

text.name: rse_guide_mods_3
text.text: Better Winch by ThundR: its winch hooks dead animals and wrecks. UniversalAutoload by loki_79: it loads them onto the trailers it supports.

text.name: rse_guide_mods_4
text.text: Front loaders, bale grabs and crane trailers all handle dead animals, but a small crane can't lift a cow.

text.name: rse_crash_hint_load
text.text: Recover the trailer, and bring the bales to a recovery point.

text.name: rse_crash_arrivedLoad
text.text: Bales on the road: %d.

text.name: rse_load_call_small
text.text: The load is small bales, so a pickup truck and your own hands can handle it.

text.name: rse_load_call_big
text.text: The load is big bales, so bring a front loader or a telehandler and something to carry them on.

text.name: rse_load_arrived_small
text.text: Carry the small bales by hand into a pickup bed, or into the trailer once it is back on its wheels. Each one that reaches a recovery point pays.

text.name: rse_load_arrived_big
text.text: The big bales need a front loader or a telehandler. Each one that reaches a recovery point pays.

text.name: rse_crash_trailerDoneBales
text.text: The trailer is in. Bring in the bales too for a %d%% bonus. If you don't, another contractor takes over after %s; the settings panel ({key:RSE_SETTINGS}) can hand them over sooner.

text.name: rse_crash_balesDone
text.text: The bales are in. Bring in the trailer too for a %d%% bonus. If you don't, another contractor takes over after %s; the settings panel ({key:RSE_SETTINGS}) can hand it over sooner.

text.name: rse_wreck_hint_deliver
text.text: Tow it on a strap ({key:RSE_STRAP}) or load it, and take it to a recovery point.

text.name: rse_flock_hornScared
text.text: All that honking has scattered the sheep. You will have to round them up again.

text.name: rse_scene_deliver

text.name: rse_ep_missing
text.text: Roadside Emergencies requires the free Emergency Pack DLC, and it isn't active in this savegame, so no calls will come. Install the pack for free from your store, then select it together with this mod when you start this savegame.
